holidays.name: World Turtle Day
holidays.description: A day to celebrate turtles and tortoises everywhere, and to encourage people to help them survive and thrive. Expect shell-themed puns, slow-paced celebrations, and lots of admiration for reptiles who carry their homes on their backs.
holidays.origin: Founded in 2000 by American Tortoise Rescue, a nonprofit organization, to increase respect and knowledge for turtles and tortoises and encourage human action to help them survive.
holidays.funFact: Turtles have been around for over 200 million years, meaning they were plodding along before dinosaurs were really getting going, and their shells are actually part of their skeleton, fused to their spine and ribs.

holidays.name: Lucky Penny Day
holidays.description: A day to pick up every stray penny you spot and treat it as a tiny token of good fortune. Bend down in public with pride and let the luck flow, even if it's only worth one cent.
holidays.origin: An unofficial observance rooted in the old superstition 'Find a penny, pick it up, and all day long you'll have good luck.' It has been listed on quirky holiday calendars as a lighthearted nod to this folk saying.
holidays.funFact: Penny superstitions vary by place: in some traditions heads-up pennies are lucky and tails-up ones should be left for someone else, and the U.S. penny costs more than one cent to produce.

holidays.name: National Taffy Day
holidays.description: A sticky, chewy celebration of salt water taffy and its stretchy cousins. It's the perfect excuse to enjoy a candy that doubles as a jaw workout and a dental dare.
holidays.origin: A food holiday observed in the United States on May 23 (taffy also gets a separate day in other calendars), celebrating the pulled-sugar candy made famous by Atlantic City boardwalk vendors in the late 1800s.
holidays.funFact: Salt water taffy contains no actual sea water. Legend says the name came from an Atlantic City candy shop flooded by a storm in the 1880s, but the story is probably a fun bit of marketing lore.

holidays.name: National Vanilla Pudding Day
holidays.description: A creamy, wobbly tribute to the humble vanilla pudding, the comfort dessert that has soothed lunchboxes and sick days for generations. Grab a spoon and indulge in smooth, nostalgic sweetness.
holidays.origin: A food observance celebrated in the United States on May 22 or 23 depending on the calendar, honoring the classic dessert that grew from centuries-old custard and blancmange traditions.
holidays.funFact: Vanilla is the second most expensive spice in the world after saffron, because each orchid flower must be pollinated by hand, and the beans take months to cure.
